# logfire_gateway_guardrail_connection (Resource)

Manages an AI Gateway connection to a Presidio service that `logfire_gateway_presidio_guardrail` resources use.

~> **Beta:** this resource is backed by a Logfire API in Beta. Its schema and behavior may change in backwards-incompatible ways before general availability.

Requires Growth, Enterprise Cloud, or self-hosted and a token with organization:read_gateway and organization:write_gateway scopes (organization:read and organization:write are also accepted). Creating or changing a connection also needs a plan with Presidio guardrails (Enterprise Cloud or self-hosted). Logfire tests an enabled connection before it saves it, so an apply fails while Presidio is unreachable. Import accepts the connection UUID or its organization-unique name.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "presidio_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "logfire_gateway_guardrail_connection" "presidio" {
  name         = "presidio"
  base_url     = "https://presidio.example.com"
  auth_type    = "bearer"
  bearer_token = var.presidio_token
  timeout_ms   = 3000
}
```

## Credentials and rotation

You supply the Presidio token through `bearer_token`. Changing it rotates the
token in place. Keep the previous token valid until the apply succeeds.

The provider sends the token only when `auth_type`, `bearer_token`, or
`base_url` changes. A `base_url` change always resends the configured token,
because Logfire never sends a stored token to a new address. A rename or a
timeout change does not resend it.

The API never returns the token. Terraform retains the configured token in
state, even though it hides sensitive values from normal output. Use an
encrypted state backend with restricted access. Terraform cannot detect a token
changed outside this configuration. The provider removes the token from the
error messages it shows.

## Connection test

Logfire tests an enabled connection against the Presidio health, analyze, and
anonymize endpoints before it stores it. It tests again when a change sets
`enabled = true`, or changes the address, the authentication, or the timeout of
an enabled connection. A rename does not run the test. If the test fails,
Logfire answers `422`, the apply fails, and Logfire keeps the previous
configuration. The error names the failed check. A disabled connection is not
tested.

Logfire Cloud accepts only public HTTPS addresses. A self-hosted instance also
accepts HTTP and private addresses.

## When changes take effect

A successful apply means that Logfire stored the change and queued a Gateway
configuration refresh. The Gateway applies the change shortly after. It does
not mean that the Gateway already enforces it.

## Failed creates

Creation is not retried automatically. A failed request can still leave a
connection stored. Check the connection list before retrying. If the name
exists, import it by name and apply the configuration again. A conflicting name
is never adopted automatically.

## Plans

Reads and deletes work on every plan that includes the Gateway guardrail API
(Growth, Enterprise Cloud, and self-hosted). Creating or changing a connection
also needs Presidio guardrails on the plan (Enterprise Cloud and self-hosted).
Without them, Logfire refuses the apply with a `403` answer. So an organization
that loses the plan can still destroy its connections.

## Deletion

Logfire refuses to delete a connection while a Presidio guardrail uses it.
When the guardrails reference `logfire_gateway_guardrail_connection.<name>.id`,
Terraform deletes them first.

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `base_url` (String) Root URL of the Presidio service, for example `https://presidio.example.com`. Logfire Cloud accepts only public HTTPS addresses. A self-hosted instance also accepts HTTP and private addresses. A change resends `bearer_token`, because Logfire never sends a stored token to a new address.
- `name` (String) Organization-unique connection name. At most 255 characters.

### Optional

- `auth_type` (String) Authentication that Logfire sends to Presidio: `none` or `bearer`. Defaults to `none`.
- `bearer_token` (String, Sensitive) Bearer token for Presidio. Required when `auth_type` is `bearer`, and not allowed otherwise. Changing it rotates the token in place. Logfire never returns this value; Terraform retains it in state. External token changes cannot be detected. After import, the next apply sets the configured token.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the Gateway uses the connection. Defaults to true.
- `timeout_ms` (Number) Timeout of one Presidio request, in milliseconds, from 100 to 10000. Defaults to 2000.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the connection was created.
- `guardrail_count` (Number) Number of Presidio guardrails that use the connection.
- `id` (String) Connection UUID.

## Import

Import a connection by name or UUID using the same organization's management token:

```terraform
import {
  to = logfire_gateway_guardrail_connection.presidio
  id = "presidio"
}
```

Or use the command line:

```shell
# Import an existing guardrail connection by its organization-unique name, or by its UUID.
#
# By name:
terraform import 'logfire_gateway_guardrail_connection.presidio' "presidio"

# By UUID:
terraform import 'logfire_gateway_guardrail_connection.presidio' "018f45c0-3cab-7b2f-a8f7-8a0b55a7ed44"
```

Import reads public configuration only. Set `bearer_token` in your
configuration; the next apply writes that token to the imported connection.
Import does not recover the existing token.
